en.title: Maria Bartiromo's Fox News Exit: Politics and Finance Clash Led to Fallout
en.summary: After years at Fox News, anchor Maria Bartiromo is out, marking the end of an era. Her departure signals a significant shift for the network's business coverage.
en.body:
The television landscape has seen a seismic shift with the departure of **Maria Bartiromo** from Fox News Media in 2026. After more than twelve years with the network, her exit marks the end of an era for viewers who tuned in for her unique blend of financial reporting and political commentary.

Bartiromo was initially brought to Fox News to bolster its business-news presence, focusing on Wall Street intricacies. However, her increasing involvement in political punditry and opinion pieces appears to have created a divide, pulling her focus away from the core financial beats that defined her early career. This pivot between the worlds of MAGA politics and Wall Street is widely believed to be the catalyst for the fallout. Her shows, including “Mornings With Maria” and **Maria Bartiromo’s Wall Street** on Fox Business, along with “Sunday Morning Futures With Maria Bartiromo” on Fox News, have undergone rebranding and will feature rotating anchors. This strategic move by Fox News Media indicates a desire to recalibrate their programming and potentially return to a more traditional business-news focus.

## Ratings Tell a Story

The viewership numbers paint a clear picture of the challenges Bartiromo's programs faced in 2026. While her shows had previously shown strength against competitors like CNBC, a noticeable decline occurred in the latter half of the year. In the third quarter of 2026, “Mornings With Maria” reportedly captured a mere 5,000 viewers in the crucial 25-54 demographic, a stark contrast to CNBC’s “Squawk Box,” which garnered 24,000. This trend continued into the second quarter, where “Squawk Box” averaged 140,000 viewers, surpassing “Mornings With Maria,” which averaged 123,000. These figures suggest that the audience may have been seeking a different kind of programming, or perhaps the perceived shift in Bartiromo’s focus impacted her core viewership.

## A New Chapter for Fox Business

The departure of **Maria Bartiromo** leaves a void that Fox News is actively working to fill. The network has already implemented changes to its schedule, with “Mornings With Maria” transitioning to “Mornings With Fox Business,” featuring a rotating cast of hosts. Similarly, **Maria Bartiromo’s Wall Street** has been rebranded as “FBN’s Wall Street,” with **Cheryl Casone** and other anchors stepping in. This move signals Fox News’ commitment to maintaining a strong presence in business news, albeit with a potentially different editorial direction. The future of these rebranded shows will be closely watched by industry insiders and fans alike, as they navigate this new era without one of the most recognizable faces in financial television.

## What's Next

Fox News Media has not yet announced long-term replacements for Bartiromo’s flagship programs. Viewers can expect continued rotation of hosts on “Mornings With Fox Business” and “FBN’s Wall Street” as the network assesses its strategy. The full impact of this significant personnel change on Fox News’ overall ratings and market position remains to be seen.
